title: Delegated Information Provision
abstract: arXiv:2603.10867v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A designer relies on an experimenter to provide information to a decision maker. The experimenter has incentives to persuade rather than merely transmit information. Anticipating this motive, the designer can restrict the set of admissible experiments, but cannot prevent the experimenter from garbling any admissible experiment. We model this situation as delegation over experiments. The optimal delegation set is obtained by comparing maximally informative experiments among those the experimenter has no incentive to garble. When the experimenter's preferences are $S$-shaped, we characterize these experiments as double censorship. Relative to the full-delegation benchmark, double censorship features an intermediate pooling region, inducing a smaller pooling region for the highest states. We show that the designer strictly benefits from imposing a nontrivial delegation set that constrains persuasion while retaining information provision

translated_abstract: 一位设计者依赖实验者向决策者提供信息。实验者具有说服（决策者）而非仅仅传递信息的动机。预见到这一动机，设计者可以限制可容许实验的集合，但无法阻止实验者对任何可容许实验进行模糊化处理。我们将这一情形建模为对实验的委托问题。最优委托集是通过在实验者没有动机进行模糊化的那些实验中，比较信息量最大的实验而得到的。当实验者的偏好呈S形时，我们将这些实验刻画为双重删失。相对于完全委托的基准情形，双重删失呈现出一个中间混同区域，使得最高状态下的混同区域更小。我们证明，设计者可以通过施加一个既约束说服行为又保留信息提供功能的非平凡委托集而严格获益。
tldr: 本文将设计者委托实验者向决策者提供信息的机制建模为“对实验的委托”问题，证明当实验者偏好呈S形时最优委托集可刻画为“双重删失”结构，并表明设计者通过施加既约束说服又保留信息提供的非平凡委托集能够严格获益。
en_tdlr: This paper models delegated information provision as delegation over experiments, characterizes the optimal delegation set as double censorship when the experimenter's preferences are S-shaped, and shows that the designer strictly benefits from imposing a nontrivial delegation set that constrains persuasion while preserving information provision.
